_description: Does the adaptive scheduler route around a node that has really failed?
Two agents on one host: their load and latency are identical by
construction (ADR-013), so recorded lease history is the only term that
can differ — which makes an idle-but-unreliable node the discriminating
case between adaptive and the baselines.
Phase 1 builds real history (docker kill for failures, real completed
MNIST training for successes) with each node running alone so every
outcome is unambiguously its own. Phase 2 measures placement share.
